- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) and forecast is flat or rising slowly, model tends to under-forecast sharp upward moves; adjust upward by 2–5% for early positive sentiment.
- After a spike in price (e.g., >90), model often over-forecasts continuation; cap forecast at +10% above peak or use mean reversion to prior 5-day average.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is rising, model often over-optimistic; reduce forecast by 3–7% for negative sentiment.
- Model consistently under-forecasts true price when sentiment is neutral or weak (0.0–0.3); apply a 1–3% upward bias for neutral sentiment.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: true price often exceeds forecast by 5–15% in first 5–7 days after spike; adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of true price.
- When sentiment history shows increasing positivity (e.g., 0.67 → 0.88 → 0.90), model tends to over-forecast; apply downward correction of 1–4% for sentiment trending upward.
- If forecast is rising steadily but true price shows mean reversion (e.g., 95 → 90 → 85), reduce forecast slope by 20–40% for 3–5 days until reversion stabilizes.
